scope: Source-backed communications operational threads distinguishing contingency readiness, expected communications constraints, and unexpected communications anomalies without inventing console decisions, root causes, event times, or Flight Director rationale.

thread_policy.purpose: Organize public communications evidence into mission-operations sequences while preserving the timing precision and event-state semantics established in Phase 2H.1.

sources.title: Artemis II Flight Day 3: Crew Prepares Cabin for Lunar Flyby
claims_used: NASA reported that the crew tested Orion's emergency communications system in deep space.

sources.title: Artemis II Flight Day 6: Crew Ready for Lunar Flyby
claims_used: Mission control expected temporary communications loss at 6:44 p.m. EDT.
Mission control expected communications reacquisition at 7:25 p.m. EDT.

sources.title: Artemis II Flight Day 6: Lunar Flyby Updates
claims_used: NASA reported Earthset at 6:41 p.m. EDT.
NASA reported that Orion entered a planned communications blackout at 6:44 p.m. EDT.
NASA reported Earthrise at 7:24 p.m. EDT.
NASA reported that the Deep Space Network reacquired Orion moments after Earthrise and restored communications.

sources.title: Artemis II Flight Day 9: Second Return Correction Burn Complete
claims_used: About two hours before RTC2, NASA reported an unexpected return-link loss of signal during a data-rate change.
The loss affected communications and telemetry transmission from Orion to the ground.
Flight controllers resumed preparing for RTC2 with the crew shortly afterward.
RTC2 occurred at 10:53 p.m. EDT and lasted nine seconds.

operational_sequence.interpretation: NASA reported that Orion's emergency communications system was tested in deep space. Public reporting does not provide a defensible exact test time.
NASA reported DSN reacquisition moments after Earthrise. No exact reacquisition UTC is assigned.

threads.name: Flight Day 9 return-link loss and recovery

operational_sequence.interpretation: The computational anchor is RTC2 minus approximately two hours. It is not an observed exact loss-of-signal time.
NASA reported that two-way communications were reestablished. Public reporting does not provide an exact recovery time.
NASA reported that flight controllers resumed preparing for the upcoming burn with the crew shortly after communications were reestablished.
RTC2 occurred after communications had been reestablished and burn preparation resumed.

guardrails: The Flight Day 6 lunar blackout is an expected operational constraint and must not be labeled an anomaly.
The reported Flight Day 6 blackout minute matching the planned minute does not imply second-level timing precision.
Reported Earthrise occurring one minute earlier than planned does not establish the exact DSN reacquisition time.
The planned 23:25 UTC DSN reacquisition must not be relabeled as an observed 23:25 UTC reacquisition.
The live DSN reacquisition remains SEQUENCE_ONLY and receives no invented UTC or MET.
The Flight Day 9 return-link-loss anchor is approximate and must not be presented as an observed 00:53 UTC loss-of-signal timestamp.
NASA's phrase 'during a data rate change' establishes context but not causation.
The supported Flight Day 9 affected direction is the return link from spacecraft to ground.
A return-link loss does not by itself establish a complete simultaneous two-way RF outage.
The exact Flight Day 9 communications anomaly duration is unknown.
The exact communications recovery time is unknown.
Two-way communications being reestablished does not identify the failed subsystem.
The public event sequence does not expose the Flight Director's decision rationale, console call history, or fault-isolation tree.
MissionLab may reconstruct evidence-backed operational sequence but must not fabricate undocumented mission-control decisions.
